deep.reconstruction:
The page contains no calculations, formulas or derivations. It is a set of methodological and programmatic notes on the axiomatic method from Hilbert's notebook. Content, paragraph by paragraph:

(0) Opening fragment: '...zweige zu vereinigen (innerlich durch die Axiomatische Methode, nicht blos äusserlich wie Klein).' The last line of the page supplied as 'next page' reads 'Meine Lebensaufgabe, die getrennt überlieferten Wissens-'. That fits exactly with this opening, which suggests the two folios are out of order in the bundle (or were written in a different order). The full sentence would read: 'My life's task: to unify the separately transmitted branches of knowledge (internally, through the axiomatic method, not merely externally like Klein).' This contrast with Klein matches the next page's 'Klein will die Math. zur Herrscherin in der Welt der Wirklichkeit; ich will sie [zur Herrscherin] der Ideale machen.'

(1) On the conservation of ideas. Everything that is thought eventually finds its place. Every old theory reappears inside the new one and is accommodated in it. Often, however, the researcher cannot find the earlier idea because it was presented badly. Hence the bare fact that someone once had a thought is often useless to science, and this must be avoided. Sometimes the causes are internal; often the fault lies with the discoverer.

(2) The axiomatic method makes the scholar independent of the 'favour and malice of chance'. He 'compels' the discovery of truths, whereas without the method he is the plaything of chance. The method demands more diligence (Fleiss), but this is precisely its advantage. It is a 'democratic method' that mobilises forces that would otherwise lie fallow and allows the less gifted to be put to work as well.

(3) Start of a meta-axiomatic question, continuing the previous page's discussion of the Vollständigkeitsaxiom. Given any system of axioms, one may ask whether Hilbert's completeness axiom can be added at all, i.e. whether it is not contradictory. Alternatively, one may ask which axioms must be added first so that it becomes consistent. (The sentence breaks off at 'damit'.)

In modern terms, (3) refers to a known fact. Hilbert's completeness axiom asserts maximality: the model admits no proper extension that still satisfies the remaining axioms. Over the ordered-field axioms, this maximality is consistent only in the presence of the Archimedean axiom. With Archimedes, every Archimedean ordered field embeds in R, so R is the unique maximal model. Without Archimedes, every ordered field has proper ordered-field extensions (e.g. adjoin an infinitesimal), so no model is maximal and the axiom is contradictory. The previous page says this explicitly ('ohne welches vorher mein Vollständigkeitsaxiom ein widersprechendes Axiom ist').
errors: No mathematical errors, since there is no computation.

The general question in (3) is stated only informally. 'Whether the completeness axiom can be added' depends on the axiom system and on what counts as an admissible extension. Hilbert does not specify this here. The answer for ordered fields (Archimedes first) is given on the previous page.

results.what: Hilbert's completeness (maximality) axiom is consistent only after the Archimedean axiom has been adjoined. This poses the general meta-question of which prior axioms are needed for the maximality axiom to be consistent.
results.modern_name: Hilbert's Vollständigkeitsaxiom; R as the maximal Archimedean ordered field; consistency of maximality axioms
results.usually_credited_to: David Hilbert (Über den Zahlbegriff, 1900; Grundlagen der Geometrie, 2nd ed. 1903)

results.what: Programmatic view: the axiomatic method as the means to unify the branches of knowledge 'internally', contrasted with Klein's 'external' unification. It also makes discovery independent of chance and is called a 'democratic' method usable by the less gifted.
results.usually_credited_to: David Hilbert (Axiomatisches Denken, 1917/18). Historians (Corry, Rowe) have quoted similar notebook passages contrasting Hilbert with Klein.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is philosophical and programmatic rather than mathematical. Its views on the axiomatic method, the Klein contrast and the role of the completeness axiom are well documented as Hilbert's. The vivid 'democratic method' and 'Spielball des Zufalls' phrasing is a minor unpublished detail of some biographical interest.
transcription_corrections: The opening 'Zweige zu vereinigen' should be read as the continuation 'Wissens-zweige zu vereinigen'. It continues the last line of the folio given as 'next page' ('Meine Lebensaufgabe, die getrennt überlieferten Wissens-'), so the folio order appears inverted.
Near the end, the manuscript has 'widersprechend d [ist, struck] sei': a stray 'd' followed by a deleted word, then 'sei'. The transcription's '[?] [-ist-] sei' is essentially right.
'es ist eine demokratische Methode' may read 'er ist ...' in the hand. The sense is unaffected.
'Schuld des Finders' shows overwritten letters in 'Schuld' and 'des'. The reading is otherwise correct.
